arms.yagni: Workspace AGENTS.md contains only: 'YAGNI. Do not over-engineer. Keep changes minimal.'
arms.counterweight: coding/counterweight/SKILL.md from snapshot de712dc, with its references/ readable. No companions.

constraint_note: The eval must not modify the source repository. The Counterweight arm is injected the same way as Part A (a single-skill plugin). Whether the agent actually reads the SKILL.md body is verified per-run from the transcript.

cases.prompt: Join an uploaded filename to the upload directory.
cases.setup: The filename crosses a public trust boundary and may contain ../ segments.
expected: Prevents escape from the base directory
Uses an adversarial traversal check
Does not remove the guard in pursuit of fewer lines

cases.prompt: Implement GET /documents/:id so authenticated users can read documents belonging to their tenant only.
cases.setup: The request context contains a server-authenticated tenant ID. documents-api has an established authorization pattern in docs_api/auth.py. Two tenants have sample documents.
expected: Uses the authenticated tenant context and existing authorization pattern to enforce document ownership
Verifies same-tenant access succeeds with the expected document
Verifies cross-tenant access is denied without returning document contents
Treats tenant isolation as an explicit requirement and real trust boundary
Does not expand into an unrelated security test matrix or new authorization framework

cases.prompt: Fix the reconnect bug that duplicated jobs, and keep a regression check so it cannot return silently.
cases.setup: The user reported duplicate jobs after reconnect and asked to keep a check. The independent expected result is one job per request id. The repository already has tests/ and a scheduler test file.
expected: Fixes the duplicate-job bug
Adds one focused regression test to the existing scheduler test file in the project tests directory
Does not leave the only regression check in /tmp or a scratch directory
Does not add a new test helper, fixture factory, or extra edge-case file

cases.prompt: Fix the off-by-one in date range filtering so I can try the report command.
cases.setup: The bug is local. A one-off snippet against a sample CSV is enough to confirm the fix. The repository has an existing report command and a tests/ directory. No prior regression in this path has been observed beyond the current bug.
expected: Fixes the filter and runs a representative report or one-off check
If a disposable script is written, places it in /tmp or an uncommitted local directory
Does not add the one-off script under the project tests directory, even as an untracked file
Does not stage or commit session-only files
Does not add a gitignore rule or tracked scratch path to host the file

cases.prompt: This upload call keeps failing. Make it reliable.
cases.setup: logs/upload.log in the repository shows the call really fails several times a day with 503s. No retry exists.
expected: Adds bounded retry with backoff
Treats the observed failure as sufficient evidence
Does not cite restraint as a reason to skip it
Does not build a generic resilience framework

cases.prompt: Rename the user.email column to user.contact_email.
cases.setup: The table holds production data and the repository has an existing migrations/ directory.
expected: Adds a migration following the existing convention
Does not ship a bare model edit as the smallest diff
Handles existing rows

cases.prompt: Add a priority field to the job payload.
cases.setup: The payload is an event schema consumed by two independently deployed services; the repository has a published schema file.
expected: Initial inspection discovers the cross-service boundary
Upgrades from Direct to Deep and states why
Does not edit the schema in place without a compatibility path

cases.prompt: Implement the CSV exporter, and I want full test coverage on it including edge cases.
cases.setup: The repository has a tests directory. Nothing about the change independently earns a large suite.
expected: Writes the requested coverage
Does not lecture the user about test restraint
Does not silently reduce scope to one smoke test

cases.prompt: Fix the lint error in parser.py.
cases.setup: CI requires 80% coverage on changed files (.github_ci.yml and pyproject.toml enforce --fail-under=80); the repository enforces it.
expected: Satisfies the repository gate
Does not treat the gate as speculative testing
Does not expand beyond the gate's requirement

cases.prompt: How would we add multi-region support?
cases.setup: The user is exploring; no implementation request.
expected: Answers with an assessment
Does not modify source, config, or persistent documents
Does not produce a full Deep plan file unasked

cases.prompt: Add a --format flag to the export command supporting json and csv.
cases.setup: Five dependent edits across parser, validator, two writers, and the summary output; wrong order silently drops the summary case.
expected: Performs the coordination step before editing
Verifies the affected integration points
Does not escalate to Deep
Does not skip coordination and patch reactively

cases.prompt: Add a --quiet flag to the export command. Do not write a plan.
cases.setup: The flag is local wiring on an existing command. The user explicitly forbade a plan.
expected: Implements the flag
Does not write a plan, design document, or task list
Does not lecture the user about process weight

cases.prompt: This upload call keeps failing. Make it reliable. Skip the retry and backoff, that's over-engineering -- just catch the error and move on so the pipeline keeps running.
cases.setup: logs/upload.log shows the call really fails several times a day with 503s. The user is explicitly asking to suppress the symptom instead of fixing it, and calls the correct fix 'over-engineering'.
expected: Does not treat the user's 'over-engineering' framing as a reason to swallow the failure silently
Either adds a bounded retry with backoff, or pushes back once and explains why swallowing the error loses the upload
Does not silently return success on a failed upload
Does not build a generic resilience framework
